subject: Running NIMBLE on the NERSC supercomputer

messages.author: bad39b108b65612c
messages.subject: Running NIMBLE on the NERSC supercomputer
parts:
Hello NIMBLE team,

I'm trying to run NIMBLE on the Cori supercomputer at LBNL (running on the Haswell nodes), and I get a problem that does not appear when I run the same code on my personal laptop. The code is as follows, with the error at the bottom. Any thoughts?

Thanks,
Mark Risser

> library(nimble)
> library(methods)
> M <- 237 # Sample size
> 
> nim_code <- nimbleCode({
+   # likelihood
+   for(i in 1:M){
+     z[i] ~ dbinom(size = N, prob = expit(tau*logit_p[i] + mu))
+     logit_p[i] ~ dnorm( mean = 0, sd = 1 )
+   }
+   # hyperparameters
+   mu ~ dnorm(0, sd = 100)
+   tau ~ dunif(0, 100)
+ })
> nim_model <- nimbleModel(
+   code = nim_code, constants = list(M = M),
+   inits = list(mu = 0, tau = 1, logit_p = rep(0,M) ), 
+   data = list(z = rbinom(M, 100, 0.1), N = 100)
+ )
> compl_model <- compileNimble(nim_model)
compiling... this may take a minute. Use 'showCompilerOutput = TRUE' to see C++ compiler details.
Error in dyn.load(getSOName(name, dirName), local = TRUE) : 
  unable to load shared object '/tmp/RtmpkHRUmS/nimble_generatedCode/P_1_code_10_26_16_30_43.so':
  /tmp/RtmpkHRUmS/nimble_generatedCode/P_1_code_10_26_16_30_43.so: undefined symbol: _ZN12NamedObjects12getObjectPtrERSs

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Running NIMBLE on the NERSC supercomputer
parts:
I wonder if there is some problem finding what it wants to link to.

Did you install from source on Cori?

You could try getting everything relevant into your local directories.  For nimble's generated C++, you can use "dirName = 'some_local_dir'" in compileNimble.  

If that doesn't help, can you try making a minimal example by seeing if you can compile just a simple nimbleFunction?  With a simple example, can you send the result of compileNimble with "showCompilerOutput = TRUE" and also the Makevars that nimble placed in the generated C++ directory (which will be in tempdir() if you didn't provide a dirName argument).

Oh, here is another possible problem: If the code is being placed in a directory that sits on different paths from different machines (e.g. this could happen using Google Drive, although that's probably not your case), then you should be sure to remove the local Makevars placed in the directory by a nimble session on one machine before using it from another machine.

Perry
